metaTitle: solana-e2e — the wallet that does what your test says
metaDescription: A Wallet Standard test wallet and Playwright fixtures for Solana dApps. Test connect, sign and send in CI, with no browser extension and no devnet.
heroEyebrow: Open source · MIT · for Playwright and Vitest
heroTitle: The wallet that does <mark>what your test says</mark>.
heroLead: A real Wallet Standard wallet your dApp lists next to Phantom — except the approve button is a line in your Playwright test. Connect, sign, send, cancel, fail, switch accounts. In CI. No extension, no devnet.
puppetAlt: A line of test code, wallet.rejectNext(), is tied by strings to a wallet popup whose Reject button presses itself; a toast says the user rejected the request and the test passed.
whyText: Four GitHub code searches (1, 2, 3, 4) return more than 100 files of hand-written Wallet Standard mocks injected into Playwright, across dozens of repositories — including Uniswap and ZeroDev — and none of them is a reusable package.
rowControls: Reject, fail, approve from the test
rowChain: Transaction checked on a local chain
playText: A small dApp and, next to it, the real @solana-e2e/wallet running in this tab in mock mode, with the buttons a test would press. Every click becomes a line of the Playwright spec below. Nothing leaves your browser unless you point the wallet at your own local chain.
howAlt: Five steps. Your dApp, in the browser page, finds the test wallet through Wallet Standard. The wallet shell in the page holds no keys and forwards each call over the Playwright bridge to a TestWallet in the Node test process, where your test approves, rejects or fails the request. In mock mode the signature goes straight back to the dApp. In rpc mode the signed transaction continues to a local Surfpool chain, is confirmed, and the test can read what landed.
howCaption: In mock mode the request stops at the TestWallet: it signs and answers, and nothing is sent. In rpc mode it continues to Surfpool. The playground above skips the Playwright bridge: the shell and the TestWallet both run inside your tab.
stepHint: Hover or tap a step to follow it in the diagram.
step1Text: Your dApp finds the wallet with getWallets(), exactly as it finds Phantom or Solflare. Nothing in your app changes.
step2Text: A tiny Wallet Standard object is registered in the page. It holds no keys: it forwards every call and returns the answer.
step3Text: Calls cross from the browser to the test process through page.exposeFunction. That is why your test can control the wallet directly.
step4Text: The TestWallet holds throwaway keys and decides what the user does: rejectNext(), failNext(), approve(), switchAccount().
step5Text: Only in rpc mode: the signed transaction is sent to a local Surfpool chain and confirmed, and localnet.getTransaction() tells you what landed.
case2: The wallet or the network fails
modeMock: Signs for real, sends nothing. For UI tests and for Vitest + jsdom, where registerTestWallet() replaces a hand-written mock-wallet.ts.
modeRpc: Signs, sends to a local RPC and waits for the commitment. With @solana-e2e/playwright you get a Surfpool chain per worker and a funded wallet per test.
ciText: Mock-mode specs need nothing but Playwright. For rpc mode, install Surfpool from its release and check the archive's sha256; the full GitHub Actions recipe is in docs/ci.md. This project's own CI runs both kinds on Linux, macOS and Windows.
limit1: The Playwright transport is a bridge to Node, so the injected wallet does not work as is in Cypress or Storybook. In-page use, like this playground, works for mock mode.
limit2: Chromium is tested in CI for the packages; this site is also tested in WebKit.
limit3: One visible account at a time, as in Phantom.
limit4: It is a test tool: never give it a key that holds real funds.
footerIssue: Your stack isn't covered? Open an issue
attribution: Built on the Solana Foundation's UI testing plan. Late injection is inspired by solana-playground's e2e fake wallet. Not affiliated with the Solana Foundation.
